definitions.explanation: A child who has become separated from their parents or guardians.

definitions.gloss: lost person, someone who is lost
definitions.explanation: By extension, anyone who has lost their way (often used playfully for adults).

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}が{迷子|まいご}になった。
{迷子|まいご}の{子供|こども}を{交番|こうばん}に{連|つ}れて{行|い}った。
examples.english: I took the lost child to the police box.

examples.japanese: お{祭|まつ}りで{人|ひと}が{多|おお}くて、{子供|こども}が{迷子|まいご}になりやすい。
examples.english: It's easy for children to get lost at festivals because of the crowds.

examples.japanese: 「{迷子|まいご}のお{知|し}らせです」と{店内|てんない}のアナウンスが{流|なが}れた。
examples.english: A store announcement came on: 'We have a lost child announcement.'

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}で{迷子|まいご}になった。
examples.english: I got lost at the station.

examples.japanese: {初|はじ}めての{町|まち}で{迷子|まいご}になった。
examples.english: I got lost in a town I was visiting for the first time.

examples.japanese: {大|おお}きなビルの{中|なか}で{迷子|まいご}になってしまった。
examples.english: I got lost inside the large building.

examples.japanese: {地図|ちず}を{見|み}ていたのに{迷子|まいご}になるなんて、{恥|は}ずかしい。
examples.english: It's embarrassing to get lost even though I was looking at a map.

examples.japanese: {大人|おとな}になっても、{知|し}らない{場所|ばしょ}では{迷子|まいご}になることがある。
examples.english: Even as an adult, you can get lost in unfamiliar places.

notes:
While literally referring to children, often used humorously for adults who are lost.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{迷子|まいご}になる (to get lost)
・{迷子|まいご}センター (lost child center)
・{迷子|まいご}のお{知|し}らせ (lost child announcement)
・{迷子|まいご}{札|ふだ} (lost child tag - worn by children at events)

RELATED EXPRESSIONS:
・{道|みち}に{迷|まよ}う (to lose one's way)
・はぐれる (to get separated from a group)

NOTE:
The kanji {迷|まい} means "to be lost/confused" and {子|ご} means "child."
